claims.text: The PGM-based nanoscale catalyst's superior ethanol-oxidation performance is governed by a dual-active-site mechanism.
Adjacent surface oxy-hydroxide species facilitate oxidative removal of adsorbed ethanol-derived intermediates.
Reducing or removing surface oxy-hydroxide species will impair activity and selectivity for complete ethanol oxidation.
The as-synthesized catalyst naturally has a mixed surface containing metallic sites and oxy-hydroxide species.
A hydrogen reductive pre-treatment can selectively lower the catalyst's surface oxy-hydroxide coverage.
Surface oxy-hydroxide species mediate oxidation of dehydrogenated ethanol intermediates.
A dynamic equilibrium between metallic PGM and oxy-hydroxide sites enhances catalytic activity and durability.
Disrupting the synergy between metallic and oxy-hydroxide sites leads to poorer catalytic performance.
Reductive pre-treatment will decrease peak current density relative to the untreated catalyst.
Reductive pre-treatment will alter product distribution and reduce selectivity for complete ethanol oxidation.
The proposed mechanism applies under acidic ethanol-oxidation conditions in which the 12-electron/12-proton transfer regime is operative.
The effect of reductive pre-treatment may differ in alkaline media or in other PGM-catalyzed reactions.
Redox cycling during operation may partially restore oxy-hydroxide coverage after reductive pre-treatment.
